title: No adult punctuation for young readers
statement: Keep adult punctuation and shorthand, such as em dashes, semicolons, any brackets, slash compounds and all-caps, out of young readers' text outside quoted source, and check it in code.
example: The ban covers punctuation that reads as adult prose to an eight- or nine-year-old, with a short list of acronyms exempt from the caps rule.
detail: A review comment on a grade 3 reading course found that machine-written em dashes made sentences harder for a child to read, and the course banned them from child-facing text. It extended the ban to semicolons, parentheses, slash compounds and all-caps emphasis, as punctuation that reads as adult prose to an eight- or nine-year-old, enforced by validators on lesson data and on text built into components (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/content-and-copy.md`, lines 18-38). The course's rule pack calls these house rules, not universal ones, and its style validator keeps semicolons only inside verified excerpts from source texts.

evidence.quote: "AI uses loads of em dashes. I would remove them entirely. It is much better for a child to see other types of punctuation and they make sentences harder to read in my opinion.
**Rule.** Same ban, same reason, extended to the punctuation that reads as adult prose to an eight- or nine-year-old.
Enforced by `scripts/validate-contracts.mjs` for JSON content (em dash and en dash) and by `scripts/validate-component-text.mjs` for text hardcoded in components
These are GRADE-3-READING house rules, not universal ones, and that is the whole reason they live in a rule pack.
The style validator preserves semicolons only inside those verified excerpts or verse lines
The six hard-won content rules (each has a gate; violations WILL bounce)
each one exists because a real defect shipped and was caught live.
Exception: quoting a play's own bracketed stage directions.
no adult note-shorthand reaches a child's screen — no parentheticals, slash-compounds or brackets
